title: Linear Equations in Two Variables and Systems
subtitle: Connect equations and graphs, compare slopes, solve systems, and model real-world situations.

isi.content: A system of equations combines two or more conditions that must be true at the same time. A solution is an ordered pair that satisfies every equation in the system.

isi.title: Example: tickets and revenue
isi.content: If \(B\) represents bench tickets and \(L\) represents lawn tickets, then \(B+L=350\) counts tickets, while \(75B+40L=19{,}250\) models the ticket revenue. The two equations describe different facts about the same situation.

items: Define each variable and include its unit or meaning.
Translate each condition into its own equation or inequality.
Choose substitution, elimination, graphing, or a calculator-assisted method.
Check the solution in every original equation and in the context.

isi.content: Keep equations separate when modeling. A count equation and a money equation should not be mixed into one relationship.

rows: Read the slope and y-intercept directly.
Model totals and eliminate a variable.
Write a line from a slope and one point.

isi.content: The slope measures the change in \(y\) for each 1-unit change in \(x\). Always attach units when the variables describe a real situation.

materi.judul: Slope, parallel lines, and perpendicular lines

items.title: Parallel
items.content: Distinct parallel lines have equal slopes: \(m_1=m_2\).

items.title: Perpendicular
items.content: Nonvertical perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is \(-1\): \(m_1m_2=-1\).

items.title: Horizontal and vertical
items.content: A horizontal line has slope 0. A vertical line has undefined slope.

isi.title: Example: perpendicular slope
isi.content: A line with slope 4 has a perpendicular slope of \(-\dfrac14\), the negative reciprocal of 4.
Do not use only the reciprocal for perpendicular lines. The sign must change as well.
The y-intercept occurs when \(x=0\). The x-intercept occurs when \(y=0\). To write a line from a point and a slope, use point-slope form.

isi.title: Example: find a y-intercept
isi.content: A line has slope \(-\dfrac54\) and x-intercept \((8,0)\). Its equation is \(y=-\dfrac54(x-8)\). Setting \(x=0\) gives \(y=10\), so the y-intercept is \((0,10)\).

items: To find an x-intercept, set \(y=0\).
To find a y-intercept, set \(x=0\).
A line with a positive slope rises from left to right.
A line with a negative slope falls from left to right.

isi.content: Substitution is efficient when one equation already gives a variable in terms of the other variable.

isi.title: Example: substitution
isi.content: For \(\begin{cases}y=2x+1\\x+y=10\end{cases}\), substitute \(2x+1\) for \(y\): \(x+(2x+1)=10\). Thus \(3x=9\), so \(x=3\), and \(y=7\). The solution is \((3,7)\).

items: Solve one equation for one variable if needed.
Substitute that expression into the other equation.
Solve the resulting one-variable equation.
Substitute back to find the second variable.

isi.content: Always check the ordered pair in both original equations, not only in the equation used during substitution.
Elimination adds or subtracts equations so that one variable disappears. You may multiply one or both equations first to align coefficients.

isi.title: Example: eliminate a variable
isi.content: For \(\begin{cases}3x+2y=12\\3x-y=6\end{cases}\), subtract the second equation from the first: \(3y=6\), so \(y=2\). Then \(3x-2=6\), giving \(x=\dfrac83\).

items: Choose the variable whose coefficients are easiest to cancel.
Keep the equation signs aligned when adding or subtracting.
Substitute the value back into either original equation.
Use exact fractions when appropriate; round only when the question asks.

isi.title: Example: no solution
isi.content: The lines \(y=3x+2\) and \(y=3x-5\) have equal slopes but different y-intercepts. They are parallel and distinct, so the system has no solution.
If one equation is a nonzero multiple of the other, the system describes the same line and has infinitely many solutions.
Translate each category separately. Counts, prices, weights, and totals usually produce different equations.

isi.title: Example: food-truck sales
isi.content: A food truck sells salads for USD \(6.50\) and drinks for USD \(2\). It sells 209 items for USD \(836.50\). If \(s\) is salads and \(d\) is drinks, then \(\begin{cases}s+d=209\\6.5s+2d=836.5\end{cases}\). Solving gives \(s=93\) and \(d=116\).

isi.title: Example: inequality system
isi.content: If a restaurant sells at least 50 items and earns at least USD \(390\) from USD \(9\) sandwiches and USD \(6\) salads, then \(s+a\ge50\) and \(9s+6a\ge390\).

items: Define variables before writing equations.
Use the correct price or rate with the correct variable.
Reject negative or non-integer counts when the context requires whole objects.
Check the result using both the total-count and total-value conditions.

isi.content: Graphing both equations shows the solution as their intersection. Desmos can also help classify a system, check an ordered pair, and inspect a table or intercept.

items: Enter each equation on a separate line.
Click the intersection point to read the ordered pair.
Check the viewing window so the relevant features are visible.
Substitute the point into both original equations.
For a real-world model, check units and whether the point is in the allowed domain.

isi.content: A graph is a verification tool. Read the equations and labels carefully before trusting a visual result.

latihan.question: Line \(k\) is \(y=4x+15\). Line \(j\) is perpendicular to line \(k\). What is the slope of line \(j\)?
discussion: A perpendicular line has the negative reciprocal slope, so \(m=-\dfrac14\).

latihan.question: The equation \(58=3x+13\) gives the perimeter of a rectangular rug. If the width is 10 feet, find the length \(x\) represented by the equation.
discussion: Therefore, the length represented by the equation is 15 feet.

latihan.question: Regular polygons A and B have a combined perimeter of 63 inches. The equation is \(3x+6y=63\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are their numbers of sides. What does the number 6 represent?
options: Each side of polygon B is 6 inches.
Each side of polygon A is 6 inches.
discussion: The variable \(y\) represents the number of sides of polygon B.
Because the equation represents combined perimeter, the coefficient 6 is the length of each side of polygon B.

latihan.question: Find the slope of \(y=\dfrac15(28x+14)+9x\).
discussion: The coefficient of \(x\) is \(\dfrac{28}{5}+\dfrac{45}{5}=\dfrac{73}{5}\), so that is the slope.

latihan.question: Keenan fills \(x\) small jars and \(y\) large jars. The equation is \(3x+7y=63\). What does \(7y\) represent?
options: The total cups of broth in large jars
The total cups of broth in small jars
discussion: The term \(7y\) means 7 units for each of \(y\) large jars.
Therefore, it represents the total cups of broth in the large jars, choice C.

latihan.question: A line has slope \(-\dfrac54\) and x-intercept \((8,0)\). Find the y-coordinate of its y-intercept.
discussion: Use point-slope form with slope \(-\dfrac54\) and point \((8,0)\): \(y=-\dfrac54(x-8)\).

latihan.question: Solve \(\begin{cases}3x+4y=-23\\2y-x=-19\end{cases}\).
discussion: Rewrite the second equation as \(x-2y=19\), so \(x=2y+19\).

latihan.question: Solve \(\begin{cases}x+y=-9\\x+2y=-25\end{cases}\). Find \(x\).
discussion: Subtract the first equation from the second: \(y=-16\).

latihan.question: Two lines are given by \(y=x+1\) and \(y=-x+9\). What is their point of intersection?
discussion: Set the two expressions for \(y\) equal: \(x+1=-x+9\).

latihan.question: A food truck sells salads for USD \(6.50\) and drinks for USD \(2.00\). It sells 209 items for USD \(836.50\). How many salads does it sell?
discussion: Let \(s\) be salads and \(d\) be drinks. Then \(s+d=209\) and \(6.5s+2d=836.5\).

latihan.question: A hamburger has 50 more calories than fries. Two hamburgers and three fries total 1,700 calories. How many calories are in one hamburger?
discussion: Let \(h\) be hamburger calories and \(f\) be fries calories. Then \(h=f+50\) and \(2h+3f=1700\).

latihan.question: A mirror and a vase have a combined original price of USD \(79\). The mirror is discounted by 25%, the vase by 35%, and the combined sale price is USD \(43\). Which system represents the original prices \(m\) and \(v\)?
discussion: A 25% discount means the mirror sells for 75% of its original price: \(0.75m\).
A 35% discount means the vase sells for 65% of its original price: \(0.65v\).
Therefore, choice C represents the system.

latihan.question: Solve \(\begin{cases}7y=10x+11\\-7y=5x-21\end{cases}\). Find \(30x\).
discussion: Add the two equations to eliminate \(y\): \(0=15x-10\).

latihan.question: Given \(3x=36y-45\), the system has no solution. Which could be the second equation?
discussion: A no-solution system needs a parallel but distinct second line.
Choice B becomes \(x=12y\), which has the same slope but a different intercept.
Therefore, the two lines are parallel and distinct, so choice B is correct.

latihan.question: Given \(\begin{cases}8x+7y=9\\24x+21y=27\end{cases}\), which point lies on both equations for every real value of \(p\)?
discussion: The second equation is 3 times the first, so both equations describe the same line.
Let \(x=p\). Solving the first equation for \(y\) gives \(y=-\dfrac{8p}{7}+\dfrac97\).
Thus, choice A gives a point on the line for every real \(p\).

additionalPractice.question: Find the slope of \(y=3x-8\).
discussion: The coefficient of \(x\) is the slope, so \(m=3\).

additionalPractice.question: Are the lines \(y=2x+1\) and \(y=2x-5\) parallel, perpendicular, or neither?
discussion: Their y-intercepts differ, so they are distinct parallel lines.

additionalPractice.question: A school sells adult tickets for USD \(8\) and student tickets for USD \(5\). It sells 120 tickets for USD \(780\). How many adult tickets are sold?
discussion: Let \(a\) be adult tickets and \(s\) be student tickets. Then \(a+s=120\) and \(8a+5s=780\).

additionalPractice.question: Find the equation of the line through \((2,5)\) with slope \(-3\).
A system has infinitely many solutions. If one equation is \(4x-6y=12\), give a different equation describing the same line.
discussion: Multiplying every term of an equation by the same nonzero number preserves its solution set.
This is a different-looking equation for the same line, so the system has infinitely many solutions.

additionalPractice.question: Two numbers have a sum of 48 and a difference of 14. Find the two numbers.
discussion: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(y\): \(x+y=48\) and \(x-y=14\).

additionalPractice.question: A restaurant sells sandwiches for USD \(9\) and salads for USD \(6\). It sells at least 50 items and earns at least USD \(390\). Write a system of inequalities for \(s\) sandwiches and \(a\) salads.
discussion: Together, these form the required system.
